title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Approving a Claim for Settlement
content:
Approval for settlement is one of the two ways in which a claim under `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims` is decided. This reference states what an approval settles and how the desk records it.

## What an approval settles

A claim file standing at documents complete, on a cover whose claim is open, is ready for a decision. Approving it fixes two things together: the sum the line settles for, and the liability measure that set that sum. For any kind of loss other than delay loss, the sum is whatever the line's settlement rules for the claim's tier produce from its records; a delay loss is governed by its own delay ceilings. An approval decides the claim; it pays nothing out by itself.

## Capability of the tool

`approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3` records the approval of a single cargo claim at a given sum, together with the measure behind that sum. With each call:

- an approval entry for the claim, bearing today's date, is added to the record the cover keeps of premium and settlements;
- the outcome of the claim file becomes approved;
- the cover's balance of settlements approved but not yet paid grows by the approved sum.

Payment is no part of the call, and the cover keeps whatever status it had.

## Invocation

Only the agent operates it: the desk agent unlocks `approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3` and then calls it with the values listed below.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `cover_id` | the cover under which the claim sits, as the cover or claim-file lookup shows it | identifier |
| `claim_id` | the claim file receiving the approval, as shown by the claim-file lookup | identifier |
| `booking_id` | the booking of the shipment the cover protects, from the booking lookup or from the cover itself | identifier |
| `container_number` | the container the claim file names | ISO 6346: four letters then seven digits, no spaces, exactly as written on the claim file |
| `amount_usd` | the sum approved for settlement | US dollars, zero or more, two decimals; kept rounded half-to-even to the cent |
| `liability_basis` | the measure that set the approved sum | one of the values below |

Values accepted for `liability_basis`:

- `package_limitation`: the loss was held to the Hague-Visby limit, with the per-package figure the larger of its two limits.
- `weight_limitation`: the loss was held to the Hague-Visby limit, with the per-kilogram figure the larger of its two limits.
- `declared_value`: the loss was held to the portion of the declared value attributable to the affected packages.
- `proven_loss`: nothing held the sum down (no limit, share, cap or aggregate), so it equals the proven loss after any uplift and deductible; it is also the value used where the invoice value of the affected packages is what limited the proven loss itself.
- `cover_limit`: the tier's cap per container held the sum down.
- `delay_cap`: one of the delay-loss ceilings held the sum down.
- `aggregate_limit`: the room left under the cover's annual aggregate cut the sum.
- `not_applicable`: never right for an approval; it belongs on premium and rejection entries.

## Return

A successful call answers with `status` "approved", `approval_event_id` for the entry just created, the `claim_id`, `cover_id`, `booking_id` and `container_number` it was given, `amount_usd` and `liability_basis` as recorded, and `settlement_payable_usd`, the approved-but-unpaid settlement total of the cover including this approval, in US dollars to two decimals. The claimant can then be given the approval reference, the sum and the measure.
